Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestAccountingChronology_test_date_now_no_chronology.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestAccountingChronology/TestAccountingChronology_test_date_now_no_chronology.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The test contains a large amount of dead code: eight `data_*` provider methods and a static `INSTANCE` field that are never referenced by any `@ParameterizedTest`/`@MethodSource`. The only executed test is `test_date_now_no_chronology`. Removing the unused scaffolding (and its now-unneeded imports) sharply improves understandability without changing what runs.Compiles cleanly. I stripped the eight unused `data_*` provider methods, the unreferenced `INSTANCE` field, and ~40 now-dead imports — leaving only the single executed `@Test`, which behaves identically (`AccountingDate.now(null)` still asserts `NullPointerException`).
